questions.stem: Why does an obligate anaerobe die when exposed to air?

options.A: It lacks catalase and superoxide dismutase to remove toxic O₂ products
options.B: It cannot make ATP without O₂
options.C: O₂ blocks its cell wall synthesis
options.D: It requires O₂ as its final hydrogen acceptor
options.E: It only grows at low O₂ tension

questions.explanation: Superoxide and H₂O₂ accumulate without SOD and catalase. B: Anaerobes make ATP without O₂ (organic or inorganic acceptors). C: O₂ does not block wall synthesis. D: Using O₂ as the hydrogen acceptor defines obligate aerobes. E: Growth at low O₂ tension defines microaerophiles.

questions.stem: In a broth culture, the viable count stays constant while the total count keeps rising. In vivo, this growth phase corresponds to:

options.C: Signs and symptoms such as fever

questions.explanation: This is the stationary phase (multiplication = death from nutrient exhaustion and toxic products), which corresponds to signs and symptoms. A: Incubation = lag phase. B: Invasion = log phase. D: Recovery = decline phase. E: The carrier state is not a growth-curve phase.

questions.stem: Griffith injected mice with live non-capsulated pneumococci plus heat-killed capsulated pneumococci; the mice died. Which gene-transfer process explains this?
questions.explanation: Competent live bacteria took up naked capsule genes from dead cells. A: No phage was involved. B: Conjugation needs live donor contact. D: Transposition moves genes within a cell. E: Lysogenic conversion needs a phage.

questions.stem: Which gene-transfer mechanism requires cell-to-cell contact but not naked DNA or phage?
questions.explanation: Conjugation uses a sex pilus between donor and recipient, with no naked DNA or phage. A: Uses naked DNA and a competent cell. B: Uses a phage. C: A lab form of transformation using naked DNA. D: Occurs in segmented RNA viruses.

questions.stem: A food handler has shed Salmonella Typhi in her stool for 6 years without symptoms. Which type of carrier is she?
questions.explanation: Chronic carriers discharge the organism for a long time; carriers are dangerous because they are asymptomatic, undetected and mobile. A: Incubatory carriers shed during the incubation period. B: Convalescent carriers shed only during recovery after illness. D: Commensals are normal flora. E: Saprophytes live free in nature.

questions.stem: Oral viridans streptococci cause endocarditis after entering the bloodstream. What type of infection is this?
questions.explanation: A commensal becomes pathogenic when it reaches a new site (mouth → heart). B: The trigger here is a new site, not low immunity. C: Zoonoses come from animals. D: Viridans streptococci are commensals, not obligate pathogens. E: A carrier has no disease.

questions.stem: A traveler has diarrhea; stool shows motile pear-shaped trophozoites with flagella and resistant cysts. Which protozoan class is this?
questions.explanation: Giardia lamblia is a flagellate. A: Amebae move with pseudopodia. B: Sporozoa (Plasmodium) are spore-forming. C: Ciliates (Balantidium) have cilia. E: Cestodes are tapeworms (helminths).

questions.stem: In DNA cloning, the insert and plasmid are cut with the same restriction endonuclease. Which enzyme then seals the insert into the plasmid?
questions.explanation: DNA ligase seals the gaps between the sticky ends, forming the recombinant plasmid, which is then transformed into E. coli. A: Reverse transcriptase copies RNA to DNA. B: Restriction endonucleases cut, they do not seal. C: DNA gyrase is the quinolone target. E: Transpeptidase cross-links peptidoglycan.

questions.stem: A helminth is leaf-shaped and flattened with oral and ventral suckers, and has separate sexes. Which is it?
questions.explanation: Leaf-shaped with suckers = trematode (fluke); flukes are hermaphrodites except Schistosoma. A: Fasciola is a hermaphroditic fluke. B, D: These are cestodes (segmented tapeworms with a scolex). C: Ascaris is a nematode, round in cross-section.
